title: DAG literacy for lab studies
dek: A directed acyclic graph is a hypothesis about missing arrows. d-separation says which independences that hypothesis implies. Adjustment is not “add all covariates.”
story: Nodes are variables. Arrows are direct causal claims you are willing to defend. No cycles. The graph is not the data. If you omit an arrow you believe exists, the independences you read off are fiction.

Three motifs: confounder (fork) X ← U → Y, mediator X → M → Y, collider X → C ← Y. Conditioning on a confounder can block a backdoor. Conditioning on a mediator removes a path you might have wanted in a total effect. Conditioning on a collider (or a descendant of one) opens a spurious association.

In TB genomics, lineage is often a confounder of mutation–phenotype associations. Hospital is often a collider if you condition on who got sequenced. “We adjusted for everything in the electronic record” is how you open colliders.
deepTitle: Backdoors, and what a DAG cannot do
deep: Backdoor criterion (sketch): a set Z blocks every backdoor path from treatment A to outcome Y and contains no descendant of A. Then adjustment for Z identifies the ATE under the usual consistency/positivity extras. This is a graphical licence, not a software option named “multivariate.”

d-separation: a path is blocked by Z if it contains a chain or fork whose middle node is in Z, or a collider whose middle node is not in Z and has no descendant in Z. If all paths from A to Y are blocked given Z, the DAG claims A ⊥ Y | Z.
A DAG does not give you SEs, functional forms, or SUTVA. It does not bless a logit. After identification, you still fit a model or a nonparametric adjustment.
Do not copy textbook DAGs from copyrighted monographs. Draw the study you ran: who was sampled, who was sequenced, who was treated, which lab measured MIC.

formulas.label: Collider warning
formulas.expression: A → C ← Y   then   A  ⊥̸  Y | C   in general
formulas.note: Conditioning on C (sequenced, hospitalised) can create a false association.

visual.caption: Three motifs in one TB-shaped drawing: lineage as a fork into mutation and phenotype, treatment as a mediator or a second cause, and “got WGS” as a collider fed by severity and by access. Adjusting for lineage can be a backdoor close; adjusting for WGS-ascertainment can be a collider open.

example.title: Conditioning on who was sequenced
example.setup: Mutation A and severe disease Y both increase the chance of WGS. You analyse only sequenced isolates. A spurious A—Y association appears even if A does not cause Y.

steps.title: Name the collider
steps.body: A → WGS ← Y (or severity → WGS ← access, with A associated with access). Conditioning on WGS=1 opens the path.

steps.title: What adjustment cannot do
steps.body: Putting WGS in a regression among sequenced people does not close this; they are already selected. You need a model of ascertainment, a different sample, or a scientific claim that WGS is independent of Y given A.

steps.title: Lineage fork
steps.body: Separately, lineage → A and lineage → Y is a backdoor. Adjusting for lineage (or PCs) is the usual close — different motif from the collider.

example.takeaway: Forks you close; colliders you do not open. “Adjust for all” does not know the difference.

choices: Blocks a backdoor path, like conditioning on a confounder
Opens a path and can create a non-causal association
Estimates the ATE by the backdoor formula automatically
check.answer: Opens a path and can create a non-causal association
check.why: That is the collider motif. Hospital, death, and “got sequenced” are the usual lab colliders.

check.prompt: A and Y independent Bernoulli(0.5). Collider C = 1 iff A=1 or Y=1. Among C=1, P(Y=1 | A=0) equals:
check.why: If A=0 and C=1, Y must be 1 (otherwise C would be 0). So P(Y=1|A=0,C=1)=1, while P(Y=1|A=1,C=1)=0.5. Selection on C manufactured an association.

whyWrong.0.5: That is the population association (none). It is also P(Y=1|A=1,C=1), not the A=0 slice.
whyWrong.0: Y is forced on, not off, when A=0 and C=1.
whyWrong.2/3: That is P(C=1)=3/4 related counts; not this conditional.

Conditioning on a common effect of two causes can open a non-causal path between those causes
WGS is a mediator of lineage
check.answer: Conditioning on a common effect of two causes can open a non-causal path between those causes
check.why: That is the WGS ascertainment problem the plate is drawn to show.
